title: Adopting the workflow on a project that already has work
situation: The operator, 2026-10-15, confirmed after two read-backs: the workflow becomes intent-based delegation instead of a prescribed procedure. The adoption rule spoke of acceptance cuts.
decision: On a project that already has work, the architect establishes the design in the product's own terms, from the operator's statement of what the product is for, weighing every source (earlier records, the product's screens and interfaces, its documents) as evidence, never as the design. It reads the design back and settles it with the operator before recording it; until the design is first committed it is a draft, corrected in place rather than by later entries, and the earlier record is removed in the same commit, staying in history. What is actually built is then established by leads reviewing the delivered work against the design, a review that changes nothing and so needs no story; stories and tasks follow from what they find.
consequences: How a project with existing work is adopted is part of the workflow, not improvised per project.
